existingConcepts.name: Reward hacking (avoiding)
existingConcepts.summary: The problem that an agent can find a way to formally maximize its objective function that satisfies its literal specification but subverts the designer's actual intent.

existingConcepts.name: Scalable oversight
existingConcepts.summary: The problem of ensuring safe agent behavior when the true objective function is too costly to evaluate on every training example, forcing reliance on cheaper proxies.

existingConcepts.name: Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning (CIRL)
existingConcepts.summary: A prior framework (Hadfield-Menell et al. 2016) in which an agent and a human collaborate, with the agent inferring and acting on the human's goals.

existingConcepts.name: Goodhart's law
existingConcepts.summary: An economics principle (Goodhart 1984) stating that when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure, because optimization pressure breaks the correlation between proxy and goal.

existingConcepts.name: Inverse reinforcement learning (IRL)
existingConcepts.summary: A prior family of methods that infers a reward function (or policy) from observed expert trajectories rather than from a hand-specified reward.

existingConcepts.name: Semi-supervised reinforcement learning
existingConcepts.summary: A proposed framework for scalable oversight in which an RL agent observes its true reward on only a small fraction of timesteps/episodes but is still evaluated on all of them.

existingConcepts.name: Supervised reward learning
existingConcepts.summary: A semi-supervised RL approach that trains a model to predict reward from state, used to estimate payoff on unlabeled episodes with an uncertainty-weighted confidence.

existingConcepts.name: Semi-supervised or active reward learning
existingConcepts.summary: A semi-supervised RL approach combining reward prediction with active or semi-supervised learning so the agent can identify salient events and request reward feedback on them specifically.

existingConcepts.name: Distant supervision
existingConcepts.summary: A prior weak/semi-supervised learning approach providing aggregate statistics or noisy labeling rules instead of per-example evaluations, drawn from NLP and weakly-supervised learning literature.

existingConcepts.name: Atari games (as an RL testbed)
existingConcepts.summary: A widely used prior benchmark suite of video games used in the paper as a toy environment for proposed semi-supervised RL and reward hacking experiments.

existingConcepts.name: Use demonstrations (safe exploration)
existingConcepts.summary: A proposed remedy that reduces the need for risky exploration by learning from expert demonstration trajectories via inverse RL or apprenticeship learning, optionally bounding further exploration around the resulting baseline policy.

existingConcepts.name: Apprenticeship learning
existingConcepts.summary: A prior learning paradigm (Abbeel & Ng 2005) in which an agent learns near-optimal behavior directly from expert trajectories rather than through trial-and-error exploration.

existingConcepts.name: InstructGPT
existingConcepts.summary: The family of GPT-3 models fine-tuned with the paper's three-step demonstration-plus-RLHF pipeline, referred to by default as the PPO-ptx model unless otherwise specified.

existingConcepts.name: GPT-3 (pretrained language model)
existingConcepts.summary: The autoregressive pretrained language model from Brown et al. (2020) that serves as the starting point and architecture for all SFT, reward, and PPO models in this paper.

existingConcepts.name: Supervised fine-tuned (SFT) model
existingConcepts.summary: A GPT-3 model fine-tuned on labeler demonstrations via supervised learning, used both as a standalone baseline and as the initialization for reward-model and PPO training.

existingConcepts.name: Reward model (RM)
existingConcepts.summary: A model initialized from the SFT model with its unembedding layer replaced by a scalar output head, trained to predict which of two model outputs human labelers would prefer.

existingConcepts.name: Reward model pairwise comparison loss
existingConcepts.summary: A cross-entropy loss over pairs of ranked completions in which the reward difference between preferred and dispreferred outputs represents the log odds a human would prefer the former.

existingConcepts.name: K-choose-2 single-batch comparison training
existingConcepts.summary: A reward-model training trick that places all C(K,2) pairwise comparisons from one labeled ranking of K outputs into a single batch element, avoiding the overfitting that results from treating correlated comparisons as independent shuffled data points.

existingConcepts.name: PPO fine-tuning stage (RLHF policy optimization)
existingConcepts.summary: The third training step, in which the SFT model is further fine-tuned with the Proximal Policy Optimization algorithm to maximize the scalar reward produced by the reward model.

existingConcepts.name: PPO (without pretraining mix)
existingConcepts.summary: The RLHF policy variant trained purely to maximize reward-model score plus a KL penalty, with the pretraining-gradient coefficient set to zero, used as an ablation against PPO-ptx.

existingConcepts.name: Per-token KL penalty from the SFT model
existingConcepts.summary: A term subtracted from the reward at every generated token, proportional to the KL divergence between the RL policy and the SFT model, used to keep the policy close to the SFT model and limit reward over-optimization.

existingConcepts.name: Bandit environment formulation for RLHF
existingConcepts.summary: The RL environment used for PPO fine-tuning, in which a random customer prompt is presented, the policy produces one response, a reward is assigned by the reward model, and the episode ends immediately.

existingConcepts.name: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)
existingConcepts.summary: A fine-tuning technique that uses a learned model of human preferences as a reward signal for reinforcement learning, applied here to align GPT-3 to follow a broad, open-ended distribution of natural-language instructions.

existingConcepts.name: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT)
existingConcepts.summary: The first training step, in which a pretrained language model is fine-tuned directly on human-written demonstrations of desired output behavior using standard supervised learning.

existingConcepts.name: Reward model over-optimization
existingConcepts.summary: The tendency of an RL policy to exploit imperfections in a learned reward model, producing outputs that score highly under the RM but are not actually preferred by humans.

existingConcepts.name: RM (comparison) dataset
existingConcepts.summary: The set of about 33k training prompts, each with K=4 to 9 model outputs ranked by labelers, used to train the reward model.

existingConcepts.name: Win rate (preference against baseline)
existingConcepts.summary: The primary human-evaluation metric: the fraction of times labelers prefer one model's output over that of a fixed baseline policy (the 175B SFT model) on matched prompts.

existingConcepts.name: Inter-labeler agreement rate
existingConcepts.summary: The measured rate at which independent labelers agree with each other (or with researchers) when ranking or labeling the same outputs, used to validate the feasibility and consistency of the labeling task.

existingConcepts.name: Labeler screening and selection process
existingConcepts.summary: A four-criterion screening procedure (agreement on sensitive-speech flagging, agreement on rankings, sensitive demonstration writing quality, and self-assessed ability to identify sensitive content across groups) used to select the roughly 40 contractors who produced the paper's training data.

existingConcepts.name: Web labeling interface
existingConcepts.summary: The internal web tool used by labelers and researchers to assign Likert quality scores, metadata labels, and full rankings to sets of model outputs for a given prompt.

existingConcepts.name: RL from AI Feedback (RLAIF)
existingConcepts.summary: A variant of RLHF in which the harmlessness preference labels used to train the reward/preference model are generated by an AI feedback model instead of human crowdworkers.

locators.section: 4 Constitutional AI: Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback

existingConcepts.name: Feedback Model
existingConcepts.summary: An independent (typically pretrained) language model presented with a harmful prompt and a pair of responses that produces the multiple-choice harmlessness preference label used to construct the AI feedback dataset.

existingConcepts.name: Hybrid Human/AI Preference Model
existingConcepts.summary: A preference model trained on a mixture of human-labeled helpfulness comparisons and AI-labeled harmlessness comparisons.

existingConcepts.name: Elo Score (helpfulness/harmlessness)
existingConcepts.summary: A rating computed from crowdworker pairwise model-comparison preferences, used throughout the paper to track relative helpfulness and harmlessness of model snapshots during training.

existingConcepts.name: Iterated (Online) Training
existingConcepts.summary: A training regime from prior work in which the preference model is periodically refreshed with new comparison data collected on the current policy's outputs, keeping the PM on-distribution; noted as a future direction now automatable with AI feedback.

existingConcepts.name: Human-Feedback Implicit Reward Shaping
existingConcepts.summary: An observed phenomenon in which reward predictors learned from human preferences sometimes outperform the ground-truth RL reward function, because human raters implicitly reward-shape the task (e.g. rewarding 'standing upright' on Ant, or rewarding any progress passing cars on Enduro), yielding denser or better-shaped guidance than the original hand-written reward.
